label: <DEL> step of length-9 sequences, boosted by early w/b/z/c
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (t=9) of length-9 sequences. Every dev activation is there, and none occur in the original or copy phases or at any other length. It fires on about 20% of L=9 delimiter steps, so (phase==1)&(L==9) gets recall 1.0 but precision 0.20. Which of those steps fire depends diffusely on the sequence content, mainly the first few original tokens: w, b, z, c (and less so a, k) at positions 0-2 raise the firing rate and magnitude, and the top examples start with w/b/z. Requiring one of w/b/z/c in orig(0..2) gives dev F1 0.46 and mass recall 0.70. The rest of the selectivity was not captured. Magnitudes are tiny (max 0.006).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: n, 1, z, l, f, y; least: g, w, t, u) and the token being output (most: b, k, a, w, j, z; least: -, 1, v, x); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=9, to_go=8, t=9.
